capitals.name: Delos
capitals.note: 'The League was centred on Delos' under Antigonid and Ptolemaic rule (undated sentence); 'most scholars however consider [Delos] to have been a full member'. Approximate coordinates of the island.

capitals.name: Tenos (Tinos)
capitals.note: 'In the Rhodian period, where Delos was not a member of the League, the synedrion assembled on Tenos.' Approximate coordinates.

correction.text: the Cycladic islands of the first League: 'Mykonos, Kythnos, Keos, and probably also Ios under Antigonus', with 'Naxos, Andros, Amorgos, and Paros ... attested under the Ptolemies' and Delos

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no League of the Islanders; checked with the gazetteer on 2026-10-19, other rows touch only 2 cells of the Cyclades region in the years sampled (Greek City-States and Macedonian Empire in 310, Ptolemaic Kingdom in 290, Antigonid Macedonia in 200, Greek City-States in 170). The page names islands, not an area; the gazetteer's Cyclades region is the stand-in, which also holds islands the page does not name as members (the page calls Samos and the southern Sporades 'possible, but unlikely'). Drawn as a client tint of Antigonus (macedonian-empire's realm until 306, antigonid-dynasty from 306) then of Ptolemy I and II (ledger).

correction.text: the Cyclades of the Second League, 'under the leadership of Rhodes in c. 200 BC'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: no territory is drawn for 259-201 (the page says 'no nēsiarchos is attested after c. 260 BC' and 'The last documents pertaining to the League date approximately to the second quarter of the century', then nothing until the Rhodian league). Delos was 'not a member' of the Rhodian league, so the Delos cell is a small excess. Per the League page (paraphrase) Andros, Paros and Kythnos stayed under Macedonian garrisons after 200. Who held the islands 260-201 is disputed on the page (free poleis per Reger; Macedonian or Rhodian influence per others), which is why the keyframe skips those years.

region.text: the Cyclades, with Delos as the centre

ledger.note: c. 314/3: Antigonus founds the League of the Islanders. 'In 314/3 BC, Antigonus I Monophthalmus sent a fleet under his nephew Dioscurides'; the League was founded 'c. 314/3 BC' under his auspices (a 306 date is often cited; Meadows argues Ptolemy II sponsored it). Antigonus's realm is inside macedonian-empire until that dossier's /ledger/63 splits antigonid-dynasty off in 306 (Antigonid dynasty page: 'Established: 306 BC'), so the counterpart of the founding and of the first eight years of the patronage is macedonian-empire, not antigonid-dynasty.

region.text: the Cycladic League under Antigonid protection

ledger.note: c. 314/3: the League under Antigonus's auspices (his realm is macedonian-empire's until 306). Recorded from the vassal's side (counterpart = overlord). It continued 'despite the defeat and death of Antigonus at the Battle of Ipsus in 301 BC'.

region.text: the League, as Antigonus's realm becomes the Antigonid kingdom

ledger.note: 306: the patron's realm becomes the Antigonid kingdom. Antigonid dynasty page: 'the dynasty first came to power after the Battle of Salamis in 306 BC' and 'Established: 306 BC' (verbatim); macedonian-empire /ledger/63 records the split. The League page says only that a fragmentary inscription 'typically dated to 306 BC' exists and that the League continued after Ipsus; it gives no 306 hand-over, so the date is the dossier chain's (confidence 2). Nothing changes for the islands.

region.text: the League under the Antigonid kings (Antigonus, then Demetrius after Ipsus)

ledger.note: 306: the League as an Antigonid client. 'Despite the defeat and death of Antigonus at the Battle of Ipsus in 301 BC', Demetrius kept the fleet and the League (paraphrase); the relation runs to 287/6. Mirrors the 314 event with the successor realm.

region.text: the Cycladic League leaving Antigonid protection

ledger.note: c. 287/6: Antigonid protection ends when Seleucus I captures Demetrius.

region.text: the Cycladic League under Ptolemaic hegemony

ledger.note: c. 287/6: the Ptolemies take over. After Seleucus I captured Demetrius 'c. 287/6 BC' the islands passed to Ptolemaic hegemony; their games were renamed 'in honour of Ptolemy I Soter and his son Ptolemy II Philadelphus'.

region.text: the Cycladic League, no longer attested

ledger.note: c. 260: the first League fades and the Ptolemaic hegemony lapses. 'no nēsiarchos is attested after c. 260 BC' (verbatim). The League page: 'The islands remained under Ptolemaic control until sometime in the middle of the 3rd century BC' and 'the Ptolemaic position collapsed completely after Andros' (verbatim fragments); the Chremonidean War page has the Ptolemaic fleet 'defeated off Cos (probably in 261 BC)', with 'a strong alternative date of 258 or 255 BC', and the Battle of Andros disambiguation page lists 'Battle of Andros (246 BC), between Ptolemaic Egypt and Antigonid Macedonia' (no result or consequence given). So the end lies between c. 261 and 246; c. 260 follows the last nesiarch and stays a bridge (confidence 1).

c. 260 to 201: the islands pass out of the League's hands and no state holds them on the pages. The League page says scholars disagree: 'suggested that the Ptolemaic withdrawal resulted in a Macedonian hegemony over the Cyclades' (verbatim fragment), Rhodes 'stepped into the power vacuum, concluding alliances with some of the islands like Ios', and 'by and large the individual Cycladic islands appear to have remained free and autonomous' (the last reading, Reger's, is the one used: free poleis, hence the greek-city-states placeholder). The Chremonidean War and Battle of Andros pages give no Cycladic consequence. In 201 'Philip V of Macedon subdued the Cyclades at the head of his fleet' (see the 200 gain). Mirrors needed: greek-city-states (eu-01) has no 260 gain of the Cyclades, and antigonid-dynasty (eu-02-a) no 201 gain of them from greek-city-states.

c. 200: the Second League under Rhodes takes the islands back from Philip V. The League was re-founded 'under the leadership of Rhodes in c. 200 BC' and 'survived until c. 167 BC'; 'In 201 BC, during the Cretan War, Philip V of Macedon subdued the Cyclades at the head of his fleet' (League page). The Cretan War page: the Rhodians 'set out to conquer all the Macedonian islands from Aegina to Rhodes' and 'The Rhodians regained control over the Cyclades and reconfirmed their naval supremacy over the Aegean' (verbatim excerpts; the page dates the battles of Chios and Lade 202 in the body and 201 in the linked titles). Per the League page (paraphrase) Andros, Paros and Kythnos stayed under Macedonian garrisons, so the Cyclades region is a slight excess. Hence the chain is free islands -> antigonid-dynasty (201) -> this League (200): the antigonid-dynasty dossier (eu-02-a) needs the 201 gain and a 200 loss, and greek-city-states (eu-01) the 260 gain and 201 loss.
c. 200: Rhodes as hegemon. Rhodes was the hegemon of the Second League (League page, paraphrased).
167: Rhodian leadership ends. The Second League 'is commonly held to have lasted until the end of Rhodian independence at the conclusion of the Third Macedonian War in 167 BC'.
167: the League of the Islanders ends. The page gives no heir; the Delos page has Rome cede Delos to the Athenians in 167 or 166 and make it a free port. Delos was not a member of the Rhodian league.

wars.name: Cretan War

zones.text: the Cyclades, subdued by Philip V in 201 and regained by Rhodes

wars.outcome: Philip V subdued the Cyclades in 201 (League page); the Rhodians 'regained control over the Cyclades and reconfirmed their naval supremacy over the Aegean' (Cretan War page) and led the Second League from c. 200.
wars.note: Span 205-200 is the Cretan War page's infobox ('205–200 BC'); the League page dates only the 201 conquest. The page dates the battles of Chios and Lade 202 in the body and 201 in the linked titles. League of the Islanders is a belligerent only in the sense of the Second League that Rhodes led from c. 200.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'Followed by further Macedonian setbacks in the Second Macedonian War (200-197 BC)'; no Cycladic border change is on the page.

certainty.note: The pages name member islands but no frontier; the Cyclades region is a stand-in, and the League was an association of island poleis.

notes: Six pages (four more opened in the fix run); the Delos page is silent on the League and is cited only for the 167/166 fate of its seat. The page treats two leagues as one institution (a first League 314/3 to c. 260 under Antigonid then Ptolemaic patrons, a Second League c. 200 to 167 under Rhodes); this dossier keeps one state with a dormant gap 259-201 and no keyframe for it, and the 260 'loss' to greek-city-states is a confidence-1 placeholder so the Cyclades are not left grey. The page's alternatives: Antigonus founded it 314/3 (text) against Ptolemy II Philadelphus (Meadows, footnote), and 306 as the often cited date. Not on the page: any member count, the Ptolemaic protectorate's start year beyond 'c. 287/6', who held the Cyclades 260-201 (the Ptolemaic naval defeats at Cos, Ephesus and Andros are dated by the page but not the Antigonid conquests that followed), the Macedonian garrisons, what happened to the islands in 167 apart from Delos. Mirrors needed: antigonid-dynasty (314 patron, 287 loss, 201 Philip V's conquest), ptolemaic-kingdom (287 hegemony, 260 end), rhodes (200 hegemon, 167 end), athens (Delos 167/166; the athens dossier ends 322). Coordinates of Delos and Tenos are approximations. Fix run (2026-10-19, after review): the patron of 314-306 is macedonian-empire (Antigonus's realm is inside it until its /ledger/63 split of 306), the hand-over to antigonid-dynasty is a 306 vassal_end/vassal_start pair (Antigonid dynasty page, 'Established: 306 BC'; the League page gives no 306 hand-over). The 260-201 gap is explained on the page by a disagreement (Macedonian hegemony suggested, Rhodian alliances with some islands, or free poleis per Reger); the greek-city-states placeholder follows the last reading and stays confidence 1, and the 200 gain from antigonid-dynasty is now confidence 2 (League page: Philip V 'subdued the Cyclades' in 201; Cretan War page: Rhodes 'regained control over the Cyclades'). The vassal_* events of this dossier are recorded from the League's side (counterpart = overlord), as elsewhere in the batch. Mirrors still needed in other batches: greek-city-states 260 gain and 201 loss of the Cyclades (eu-01); antigonid-dynasty 201 gain of the Cyclades from greek-city-states, 200 loss to this League, and the 314-306 patronage now under macedonian-empire (eu-02-a); ptolemaic-kingdom has no dossier on the mount yet (287 hegemony, c. 260 end).
